title: Trevor Philips
text: Trevor has had very positive responses from many fans of ''GTA V'' and professional video game critics about his "fuck off!" personality, and extreme behavior. Trevor's grand appearance during the GI demo is considered an unforgettable one and sets up the character nicely, (the camera is zoomed in on Trevor's face but then zooms out to show him sitting on the toilet fighting constipation while yelling the famous quote, "''I need a fucking midwife for this thing!''").

title: Trevor Philips
text: "''Trevor appeared to us pretty much out of nowhere as the embodiment of another side of criminality – of freedom, and of doing what you want. If Michael was meant to be the idea of some version of criminal control – or some sort of bourgeois criminal who tries to go straight and gets sucked back in – what about the guy who didn't do that? What about the opposite guy? What about the guy who just says ‘fuck off’ every moment, is relentless, doesn't want to stop taking drugs, doesn't want to stop partying, doesn't want to be told 'no' by anyone, and just completely revels in chaos?''"

title: Trevor Philips
text: "''Trevor was the other side of the GTA coin, I suppose. He's the person who's driven purely by desire, resentment, no thought for tomorrow whatsoever, completely id rather than ego-driven. Constant partying, constant madness. The only thing he doesn't want to do is stop. He wants to keep going and ride it all to the end. Won't take an insult from anybody. Kills without remorse, like a true psychopath, but very sentimental for the right reasons when it suits him. That seemed like another side of the kind of GTA coin or the GTA world, but very rarely as the protagonist. That seemed an interesting guy to have as a protagonist. Very unlike anyone we've had in a game before. If you began to develop him and Michael and their previous relationships... We wanted this feeling where you start off thinking one's good and the other's awful. Then you get spun the other way. Then you get spun back the first way, until you can't decide.''"

title: Trevor Philips
text:
*"''Now normally, I have that whole 'beggars can't be choosers, take anything you can when it comes to love' attitude. But, when the love takes the form of someone shitting on my business, I'm not fucking interested. What's your problem, huh? Why aren't you scared of me?''" – Trevor during his first meeting with a male .
*''"Well, why we don't just ask him then, huh? Hey, hey, cowboy, do you mind that I fucked your old lady? Sorry, what was that? What? No, no? You don't mind? Oh, because you're a dead man, and the only sentient part of you left is this little bit of brain in the gristle on the end of my boot? Well, thank you very much, cowboy."'' – Trevor to [[Terry Thorpe|Terry]] and [[Clay Simons|Clay]] after Johnny's death.
*''"Now go, I need to meditate. Or masturbate. Or both..."'' – Trevor [[Nervous Ron|talking]] with Ron.
*''"I hear a little bird tellin' me that they have a bit of a problem, since one of them is going to have to be surgically removed from the skull of the other. Fuck you guys and fuck them!"'' – Trevor after discovering that the O'Neil Brothers took his contract.
*''"I don't know what I want. It's a bit, well, like pornography or a perfect turd, I can't quite describe it, but I'll know it when I see it."'' – Trevor [[Scouting the Port|talking]] with Floyd.
*''"Massage me, motherfucker!"'' – Trevor to Floyd.
*''"Hey, by any chance did you catch crabs at that conference? I hear those conferences are regular little fuck fests, eh."'' – Trevor to Debra.
*''"Exactly. Everyone's so hung up on appearances in LS, you start to forget who you are. And if you ain't who you are, who the fuck are you?"'' – Trevor to [[Ron Jakowski|Ron]] in [[Minor Turbulence]].
*''"This is my life's work. I mean, since I was a little kid I-I dreamt big, y'know? I've always wanted to be an international drug dealer and... weapons trader, alright? So I'm begging you, let's make this happen."'' – Trevor to [[Tao Cheng]] and his [[Cheng's translator|translator]] in [[Crystal Maze]].
*''"I think the only thing that didn't go as PLANNED was me showing up on your doorstep ten years later, Mikey! I mourned YOU!"'' – Trevor upon uncovering the truth about [[Brad Snider|Brad]] in [[Bury the Hatchet]].
*''"You're looking at it rationally – there are people who are useful to you, and people who ain't, and the people who ain't got to go. Me. I'm not rational. I don't care if you're useful or not. I feel like taking you out, Devo, so that's what I'm doing."'' – Trevor to [[Devin Weston]] before killing him.
*''"I think I would recognize my own underwear, now give them back!"'' – Trevor to a random bodybuilder on Vespucci Beach.
*''"Never eat Indian people!"'' – Trevor after vomiting in a public fountain.
*''"Well, loyalty is important. Let me put it that way... loyalty is important. I mean, that's the only code you need. Loyalty is the code. Kill strangers. Protect friends. Eat enemies."'' – Trevor to Franklin, while hanging out.
*''"I'm not scared of you anymore! I'm a big boy now!"'' – Trevor to Clowns in [[Grass Roots - Trevor]].
*''"Look, this is all I've got, alright? I've had a tough upbringing! My daddy was not nice to me! Okay? Look, Debra, I love you, and I love you too, Floyd! Why can't we all just be together, huh?! You can have Mondays through Thursdays, you can have the weekends, alright?! I know that's not normal, but in this crazy, crazy world, is normal so good?! Huh?! Look, Debra! Floyd! Will you marry me?!"'' – Trevor to Floyd and Debra.
*''"Ron! Ron! I'm back...And bring me my coffee or I'm gonna cut your arm off!"'' – Trevor during [[Minor Turbulence]]
*''"And they damaged my stuff. They smash up my home. Damage my soul. Look at this... This, this, this, this statue here of Impotent Rage. This fucking meant more to me than Johnny K meant to anyone! And they smashed it! Those pathetic, midlife crisis, hog-riding, shaven-headed, fruity leather-chap-wearing fucking assholes!"'' – Trevor expressing his anger during [[Nervous Ron]] mission.
*"''He got a little angry, which meant I got a little angry''" – Trevor to Michael before telling him he kidnapped [[Martin Madrazo]]'s wife.

title: Trevor Philips
text:
*Trevor's character is somewhat similar to that of from ''''.
**Trevor shows loyalty to Michael, who is similar to . Michael's kids also call Trevor 'uncle', much like Tony's kids do Paulie.
**Trevor's 'Grown Out' hairstyle resembles that of Paulie.
**Both have uneasy relationships with their mothers.
**Both are seen sniffing women's underwear.
**Both characters are referred to as being "psycho" and other similar terms.
**Both get angry when their families' native countries are insulted (Trevor is Canadian and Paulie is [[Italy|Italian]]).
**Trevor owns a strip club and used it as a base for his criminal operations, similar to how the DiMeo crime family used the strip club.
*Trevor's dedication to his mother and the fact that he can wear dresses may be a reference to from 's 1960 horror film ''''.
*In the [[Rush Casting Call]], Trevor's character name was labelled as "Simon". Interestingly, Steven Ogg also portrayed a character named in ''''.
*Trevor's personality is likely based on the character Waingro from the movie ''''.

title: Trevor Philips
text: *Trevor's initial backstory was that he grew up in the rural American backwoods. However, when [[Canada|Canadian]] actor [[Steven Ogg]] was hired to voice the character, the producers decided to work Ogg's thick Canadian accent into the character. As a result, Trevor's origins were changed, and the character was now purported to have grown up "near the Canadian border". Trevor's Canadian origins are something of an in-joke throughout the game, as numerous characters express anti-Canadian sentiment. *While [[Michael De Santa]] and [[Franklin Clinton]] have the ability to kindly greet [[Pedestrians|people]] when the player presses , Trevor on the opposite hand can only taunt people, leading them to either run away or fight him. **Trevor also gives unique taunts to [[:Category:Gangs in GTA V|gang members]], overweight people, [[Tramps|homeless people]], hipsters, the [[Los Santos Police Department (HD Universe)|LSPD]] and the elderly. *Trevor can trigger unique responses from pedestrians by passing by them. Most of them are of a fearful nature commenting on his looks and hygiene. He can still receive these responses even if the player controls Michael or Franklin and hangs out with Trevor, in which case Trevor can respond back with insults. *In Trevor's trailer, there is a flag on the wall with the emblem of a special forces unit called the [[Special Airborne Unit]] with the Latin motto 'Confide Nemini'. This could have been the unit that he was training in before his discharge. Trevor can also buy a Lonewolf jacket from [[Clothing in GTA V/Suburban|Sub Urban]] which has the same logo on the back. *Trevor gives several hints across the game that he enjoys older women. In the mission [[Hood Safari]], if Trevor uses the [[Seashark]] that the stunt woman is tied on, he says "that's why I prefer older women" when she starts to scream. In the [[Strangers and Freaks]] mission [[Vinewood Souvenirs - The Last Act]], he says to [[Al Di Napoli]] that "older women should be appreciated, like a fine cheese". [[Patricia Madrazo]], the only woman in the game apart from his [[Mrs. Philips|mother]] that he really likes and respects, is clearly older than him; she is later stated by Trevor to be 57. [[Mary-Ann Quinn]] is younger than him, but still pushing 40, and he develops an instant attraction to her; he does the same to [[Molly Schultz]] as well. On the other hand, Trevor can optionally set up [[Booty Call|booty calls]] with [[Ursula]], a random character who is much younger than he is, as well as strippers from the [[Vanilla Unicorn]] who likewise are in their twenties. *He sometimes refers to his [[Trevor Philips Enterprises|company]]'s name as "Trevor Philips Industries" and "Trevor Philips Enterprises". Rarely, he can be heard saying "TP Conglomerate" like in the mission [[Scouting the Port]]. *Trevor's favorite radio station is [[Channel X]]. This can be assumed because during the mission [[Crystal Maze]], upon hearing [[Non-Stop-Pop FM]] or "" on [[Los Santos Rock Radio]] playing, he exclaims that "the music's all wrong" and switches to Channel X which he says is "what [he's] looking for". Despite this, Los Santos Rock Radio plays on the radio in his trailer, [[Floyd Hebert|Floyd]] [[Floyd's Apartment|apartment]], and his [[Ace Liquor|liquor store/meth lab]], suggesting he somewhat likes the station, but to a lesser extent than Channel X. **Judging from in-game animation, he also likes [[Rebel Radio]]. *[[Switch Scenes|Switching]] to Trevor from another character is a crapshoot. While Michael and Franklin will usually be involved in mundane tasks or simply driving around, Trevor is often in the midst of some [[Switch Scenes#Trevor Philips|unusual activities]], from asking a homeless man if he would like a handjob to waking up drunk in a dress at the peak of Mount Gordo. One frequent scenario is being chased by the police; this further disables switching characters until the wanted level is dealt with. *The only time Trevor ever mentions his deceased brother [[Ryan Philips|Ryan]] is when talking to a [[Graham|man dressed as a zombie]] on [[Vinewood Boulevard (HD Universe)|Vinewood Boulevard]] in which he comments ''"You remind me of my brother Ryan."''. *Trevor sleeps for the longest time of all the three [[protagonist]]s. When saving the game as Trevor, the game skips ahead 12 hours. Franklin sleeps for 8, while Michael sleeps for 6. One of the withdrawal symptoms of [[methamphetamine]] is sleepiness and fatigue which may explain why he sleeps the longest. *[[The Lost MC]] bikers will always attack Trevor whenever he passes by them. *If the player visits the in-game website PsychicShoutout and speaks with Miss Marcy as Trevor, he will hold his own penis and ask her what he is holding in his hand. She will describe his penis as small, frayed with over use and special for him, making Trevor impressed that she guessed right. Miss Marcy will then ask Trevor if his mother is proud of him, which immediately makes Trevor very angry at her for mentioning his mother, he asks what she knows about his mother and if she is alive or coming through Miss Marcy. Miss Marcy then ends the conversation. *Sometimes, the LSPD can be heard taunting Trevor personally over the loudspeaker, shouting things like ''"Get down right now, Trevor!"''. This implies that he has had enough run-ins with the LSPD for them to know him personally. *Ironically, despite being the most violent of the trio and the most willing to take risks, Trevor fulfills the "less" dangerous role in three of the four [[Heists in GTA V|heists]] in which he is involved. In the freighter option of [[The Merryweather Heist]], he stays behind with the [[Submersible|mini-submarine]], while Michael and Franklin fight the [[Merryweather Security|soldiers]]. In [[Blitz Play]], he stays back and provides cover again, while Franklin and Michael fight the police officers and in the obvious approach of [[The Big Score (GTA V)|The Big Score]], he flies the [[Frogger (TPE)|chopper]] to transport the gold, while Michael simulates a robbery in the [[Union Depository]] and Franklin actually steals the gold. This could be because of his potent distrust in Michael, fearing that he could be betrayed once more by his former partner if he didn't have eyes on him at all times. However, it could simply be due to him being the most-skilled pilot of the group, as he was military-trained. **In Blitz Play, he says ''"As long as I am not on the ground when the shit goes down."''. *Sometimes, when visiting [[Sandy Shores]] as Franklin or Michael, he can appear in his [[Trevor's Trailer|yard]] drunk, [[drinking]] alcohol and throwing [[grenades]]. If the player switches to Trevor while he is doing this, the grenades will disappear, and he will have sobered up. **The [[Los Santos County Sheriff|police]] will not react to him, even if he kills a sheriff. Also, Trevor will not stop throwing grenades, even if the player is in the way. Interestingly, his grenades will knock cars and trucks around, as the grenades are scripted to land in the same place. *During [[Friendships in GTA V|friendship activities]] with Franklin, Trevor reveals that if he was not expelled from school, he may have had a profession in the arts, such as a singer or an artist. He claims that he has something "very big" to tell the world but does not quite know what it is. *Trevor has a spade tattoo on his right forearm and a dagger tattoo on his left hand in his [[Grand Theft Auto V/Artwork|artworks]], despite not having them in the final game. It is possible to buy two dagger [[Tattoos in GTA Online|tattoos]] in the game, one for each forearm. The dagger on his right forearm in the game is the one that is pictured on his left one in the artwork, and the dagger on his left forearm in the game has a dragon around it. **One of the daggers looks exactly like the knife in '''', another game made by [[Rockstar Games]]. *Only one of Trevor's default tattoos can be removed: "R.I.P Michael". This was most likely done so that players could remove/replace the tattoo once Trevor discovered that Michael was still alive, and after Trevor found out about [[Brad Snider|Brad's]] death in [[Bury the Hatchet]], the players would place the "Betraying Scroll" tattoo on his left chest. *Trevor's signature color is orange. **The selection of the protagonist's signature colors may also be a reflection of the character's personalities and/or their individual story arcs. Orange is the color of amusement, madness and danger, reflecting Trevor's chaotic and eccentric lifestyle, his destructive habits, his persistent dark humor, and his general tendency to be a public menace. *Trevor can wear Patricia Madrazo's clothes, as they are found in his [[wardrobe]]. They could be a symbol of remembrance to him of Patricia or suggest he likes wearing women's clothing, as he can also wear dresses. *Unlike Michael and Franklin, on the [[Rockstar Games Social Club|Social Club Overview]] page, Trevor's business card amusingly states "''None of your business card''". *Despite being scared of clowns, Trevor can get a large tattoo of a clown on his torso with some text reading "Sleep Tight!". *It is possible to see Trevor's genitals when he is wearing a dress, making it the second instance in ''Grand Theft Auto'' history that genitalia are exposed, after [[Thomas Stubbs III]] during the [[Cutscenes|cutscene]] of [[Politics]] in . They are also briefly seen in the opening cutscene of [[Scouting the Port]], as well as being able to be seen in [[By the Book]] if the player starts the mission as Michael. *When following him as Franklin or Michael for too long, he will headbutt either of them. **This is in contrast to Michael and Franklin, when following them as controlling another protagonist, Michael or Franklin (depends on who is being followed) will punch whoever is being controlled. *There are several instances where Trevor's death is foreshadowed, by others or even himself — all of which reference the alternate ending mission [[Something Sensible]] in some way. **In one of his dialogues when talking to a random pedestrian, or when driving a vehicle and flipping off a random driver, he may say "''Why hasn't someone sensible shot you yet?".'' **During the mission [[By the Book]], if Trevor chooses not to inject [[Ferdinand Kerimov|Kerimov]] with the adrenaline shot after he loses consciousness from being tortured, a unique "Mission Failed" cutscene will play where [[Steve Haines]] will notice that Mr. K has died, and after a brief argument with Trevor, he will end the confrontation saying "''Because soon, I'll put an end to your little charade...''" before leaving. This is a hint towards Steve's view of Trevor as a liability and thus the reason he ordered Franklin to kill him, deeming him too "uncontrollable" and "insane." **In , during the [[Heist Setups|heist setup]] mission [[Series A - Steal Meth]], Trevor will warn the player after stealing the [[Phantom|tanker]] that the meth juice inside is really flammable, and to try and not let the [[O'Neil Brothers]] shoot it too much. He then brushes off this danger with the sarcastic remark "''But, hey, it's your flaming carcass, not mine.''". *If Trevor meets Franklin before [[The Merryweather Heist]], Franklin will become hostile and shoot Trevor, and vice versa. *If Trevor meets Franklin after [[The Time's Come]], Trevor will refer to Franklin as a "traitor" and threaten him. *When viewing Trevor's "Mullet" [[Barbers in GTA Online|hairstyle]] in the mirror, his bald spot has more hair on top, similar to how he wore his hair in [[2004]]. *According to himself, he was dead for five minutes after putting an axe into a power cable.7329|Video}})}}}}}} *Trevor is the least likely to change clothes automatically when switching characters, showing his little regard for hygiene or cleanliness. *Trevor holds the position as the only GTA protagonist to have canonically killed another protagonist, as he murdered [[Johnny Klebitz]], protagonist of . *Trevor is the protagonist who encounters most other protagonists in the series, that being four (Michael De Santa, Johnny Klebitz, Franklin Clinton, and the ''GTA Online'' Protagonist). *Unique to Trevor, he expresses anger when calling a phone number only to hear the "busy" tone, yelling quotes such as "Bullshit!" or "Well, I'll be fucked!". These quotes are the same as when the player runs out of ammunition for a weapon, or when an angry NPC is trying to attack him while he is in a vehicle. *In the opening cutscene for [[By The Book]] in which Michael arrives first, Trevor briefly talks about his shape as result of his meth use, claiming "I could still take you, sugar tits". Originally, Trevor instead; however, this was dubbed over with "sugar tits" in the final version of the cutscene audio (mastered version). Leftovers of this dialogue can be found in individual scripted mission audio files for the mission, as well as on YouTube.{{Ref |name = bythebook-nword |type = audiosample |ref = FBI3_ADAE_01 |filepath = \x64\audio\sfx\SS_FF.rpf\fbi3.awc |image = BytheBook-GTAV-Audio-FBI3_ADAE_01.wav }}

title: Carbonizzare
text: The [[Grotti]] '''Carbonizzare''' is a two-door sports car appearing in and , and due to appear in .

title: Carbonizzare
text: The Carbonizzare's presence in was first spotted in the game's [[Grand Theft Auto VI/Trailers#Trailer 1|first trailer]], where a red Carbonizarre can be seen parked along [[Shore Drive]] in [[Vice Beach (HD Universe)|Vice Beach]] (0:31).

title: Carbonizzare
text: The Carbonizzare's design appears to primarily draw inspiration from the , incorporating features from the , mainly the car's retractable hardtop feature, as the V12 Zagato does not feature any folding roof mechanism, but also the shape of the rear windshield and the mirrors. The headlights, front bumper air intakes, and integrated LED daytime running lights closely resemble those of the . Furthermore, the tail lights seem to be derived from the , while the diffuser shows some resemblance to that of the .

title: Carbonizzare
text:
The Carbonizzare takes on a simplistic, but modern and sporty design, with LED daytime running lights lining the headlights as well as the front intakes. Numerous elements of the car are covered in carbon fiber, such as the rear vents & diffuser, as well as the wing mirrors. The rear of the car prominently displays the Grotti name as chrome badging across the trunk lid, between a set of circular twin brake lights. This hood/bonnet opens to reveal the engine bay and a built-in strut brace.

The car used the "Schafter Brown" interior, a derivative of the interior found on the [[Schafter (second generation)|Schafter]] and the [[Tailgater]] with a unique tan color. features a tan coloured interior, in a similar manner to the [[Super Diamond]].

The car only utilizes the primary color slot, used for the body and the interior stitching. It uses a set of wheels similar to the "Hypher" high-end rims available in [[Los Santos Customs]].

title: Carbonizzare
text: The Carbonizzare appears in the [[Grand Theft Auto VI/Trailers#Trailer 1|first trailer]] for , retaining most of its previous design, but with updated, higher-quality taillight textures and a subtly thicker, more conventional fender-to-taillight junction.

title: Carbonizzare
text:
The Carbonizzare is a fairly middle-of-the-road Sports car, with good acceleration and top speed. Its handling is very well balanced between understeer and oversteer, making it easy to drive and hard to spin out. Understeer is more pronounced at higher speeds but is easily manageable. Crash deformation is acceptable compared to other Sports cars, but it won't take many collisions for performance-reducing damage to occur. While very well balanced in its entirety, the Carbonizzare's lack of distinction makes it a fairly meager choice for a racing vehicle. Overall, the Carbonizzare is a solid choice for newer players but lacks potential in more skilled hands.

This car features a front-mounted modelled twin-cam inline-4 engine with a cylindrical air filter mounted on its intake manifold. Despite being modelled as a inline-4, it sounds more like a high revving, flat-plane V12. It has a 6-speed transmission and a front engine, rear wheel drive layout.

title: Kuruma (Armored)
Kuruma (Armored)
text: The [[Karin]] '''Kuruma (Armored)''' is a vehicle featured in as part of the [[GTA Online: Heists|Heists]] update.

title: Kuruma (Armored)
text:
The vehicle is essentially a [[Kuruma]] fitted with bulletproof armor panels on the roof and the cabin and protective frames over the lights, as well as bullet resistant windows that rarely shatter under the fire of small guns.

The car received minor cosmetic changes on the body, where the badges and the roof brake lights were removed, and the original chrome details were replaced by blacked-out ones. The rear bumper has big-bore exhausts and a spoiler with bolted-on details on the sides, while the interior features a roll cage.

Colour distribution is similar to the normal Kuruma, having a primary colour for the body and the interior stitching. However, the secondary colour affects the armor plating, the protective frames on the lights, the details on the front fenders and the roll cage. The wheel design is shared with the normal Kuruma, albeit painted in black.

title: Kuruma (Armored)
text: The Kuruma has a modeled twin-cam straight six engine, placed longitudinally in a front engine, all wheel drive layout (a rather unique distribution of 1/3 of the engine power to the front wheels and the rest to the rear wheels). According to [[Southern San Andreas Super Autos]], the car has a six-speed gearbox, a top speed of 147mph and weighs 2,866lbs. The Kuruma features a turbo dump-valve sound effect by default, although the player can add another turbo for a significantly higher acceleration.

title: Kuruma (Armored)
text: The performance is slightly different from the normal Kuruma. While it has slightly less traction (though still very good due to the normal Kuruma's high traction), slightly weaker brakes, and slightly lower acceleration and top speed, it makes up for these shortcomings in its durability against collisions and gunshots; against most firearms, it is about three times as durable as the normal Kuruma. It is equipped with bullet resistant windows that will rarely shatter if shot at, though bullet holes will appear. This can protect the players inside the vehicle, as a bullet shot through the narrow panels will not damage the player's [[health]] to a great extent, though players need to be mindful that their vision is significantly obstructed in [[First-Person View|first-person view]]. They cannot throw explosive weapons and the driver cannot shoot their gun behind the car as they can only fire forwards, both being significant disadvantages. Likewise, the rear passengers cannot shoot forward. The only thing the Armored Kuruma is truly vulnerable to is explosions (which instantly destroy the vehicle) and high-caliber weapons (the [[Insurgent Pick-Up]]'s mounted gun takes it out in 16 seconds aimed at its engine), even with its armor maxed out, though its armored panels can resist some explosive rounds from a [[Heavy Sniper Mk II]]. Therefore, players will have to be careful around explosions when using this vehicle. In addition, compared to the normal Kuruma, its engine produces much more torque, allowing it to ram through traffic harder and more easily than most vehicles of similar size, but at the cost of speed. Finally, the Armored Kuruma is immune to crash deformation, which is an advantage in that the wheels will never lock from any crash, but also a disadvantage in that the player(s) inside may not know how damaged the Kuruma is until it starts burning.

title: Kuruma (Armored)
text: Because of the armor, the vehicle is noticeably heavier than the normal Kuruma (an extra 1,700 kilograms of mass is added to the 1,500 kilogram stock), and that predictably means it has more understeer. It is also slightly harder to roll on uneven terrain, although this is not very noticeable, as the normal Kuruma is quite good off-road. Furthermore, it is harder to cause a spin out due to the Armored variant having better handling than its normal counterpart. In high speed turns, the Armored Kuruma is less likely than the stock to lift itself onto two wheels and potentially flip over. Driving off-road is one of the best of its class, and with very strong traction, it fares well climbing hills.

title: Kuruma (Armored)
text: Pre-modified variants of the Kuruma (Armored) can appear as a random target vehicle in the [[Moving Target]] [[Freemode Events|Freemode Event]], as part of the [[Freemode Events Update]]. The first set cannot be recreated in [[Los Santos Customs]] or any other [[Mod Garages|mod shop]] as it has a unique primary colour.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: The Sticky Bomb is a -like explosive with a tripwire-triggered mechanism taped onto it. When thrown, the bombs emit a steady beep and a yellow light flashes. When activated the beep rises in pitch and speed, and the light turns red, then after less than a second, they detonate.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: The Sticky Bomb gains a new design and is now comprised of two M112 C-4 explosive sticks with a remote-controlled time bomb taped onto it. There is a small red light attached to the device to help mark it when placed and, like in its previous iteration, emits a steady beep, though not as noisy.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: The Sticky Bomb has the primary advantage of being a controlled explosive and having a controlled detonation, making it useful for timing explosives when the target is on the blast radius, which is similar to that of a [[Grenades|grenade]]. As expected from its name, they can be thrown and stick to any surface they hit, which gives it another advantage over grenades as there is no need to be concerned they might bounce away from the target and either miss or worse, come back to the player and kill them in the process. Unlike [[Satchel Charges]] from , these bombs do not stick to people. They can then be detonated by pressing Down on the D-pad or shooting them.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: Up to 10 Sticky Bombs (2 in multiplayer) can be placed; throwing out the 11<sup>th</sup> (3<sup>rd</sup> in multiplayer) will cause the first one to disappear. The bombs have a 90 second fuse, so if an armed bomb is left undetonated for 90 seconds, it will automatically detonate. If the player is in a vehicle of any kind and they try to hold the sticky bomb until it detonates, it will not explode even after 90 seconds has gone by. It will start to beep slowly, and after about 60 seconds the beeping will get faster, but it will still not explode. If the player throws it out after holding it for a long time, the timer will reset as it is thrown out, so holding the bomb will not affect the time it takes to detonate.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: Because of the beeping sound and the yellow light, the player might take difficulties to take out other players, as they can see or hear the bomb and they might either avoid passing over there or destroying them with another weapon, so the player may need to find alternatives. One of the best methods is that the player just need to open a car door (preferably to the side other players do not use to enter the vehicle) and stick the bomb to the inside of the door, so when the door closes, the bomb is inside the vehicle. This prevents other players from seeing the bomb.

title: Sticky Bombs
text:
The Sticky Bomb is no different from the ''TBOGT'' iteration. Although they cannot stick to pedestrians in Story Mode, they can stick to them, as well as other players in Online. The limit for placed bombs has been amplified to 20 (5 in ). When the limit is reached, a message appears on the screen indicating it, and, like in ''TBOGT'', the first one disappears when the 21<sup>st</sup> (6<sup>th</sup> in ''GTA Online'') is placed. Unlike in ''TBOGT'', they will not explode over time.

Sticky Bombs can be used as a cheaper replacement for the [[car bomb]] in ''GTA Online''. The player just need to open a car door (preferably to the side other players do not use to enter the vehicle) and stick the bomb to the inside of the door, so when the door closes, the bomb is inside the vehicle. This prevents other players from seeing the bomb, by applying the car bomb trick mentioned above, they can ensure no other players can see them.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: The weapon can be useful in drive-bys, due to the fact it deals a large amount of damage, can stick to any vehicle, and can be detonated at any time (which allows them to be used somewhat like landmines). However, the player must be careful to ensure that their own car does not get caught in the blast radius, if using them against a vehicle in close proximity. Another factor to take in mind is how fragile they are, as shooting them will cause them to explode. If they are placed onto a vertical surface and rammed by a car, they will detonate. When armed, the Sticky Bomb will explode when shot from the player's hand; the vehicle they are inside will be destroyed, regardless if the vehicle has any sort of protection to explosions.

title: Sticky Bombs
text: Sticky Bombs are more damaging against tanks, inflicting 28.57% more than any normal explosion. The [[Rhino (HD Universe)|Rhino]] (in free roam) can be destroyed with three Sticky Bombs, while the [[TM-02 Khanjali]]/[[APC]] can be destroyed with six Sticky Bombs.

title: Sticky Bombs

title: Entity Xf
Entity Xf
text: The [[Pegassi]] '''Zentorno''' is a two-door hypercar featured in and as part of the [[High Life Update]].

title: Entity Xf
text: The Zentorno is heavily based on the , evident in its unique silhouette, side profile, distinctive mirrors, hexagonal rear vents accompanied by dual roof vents, and the characteristic front fascia. Additionally, its design is significantly influenced by the , as reflected in its grille, sharper front end, hood vents, rear vents, roof vent design, diffuser, and the painted accents on the wheels and front diffuser. The "Racing Spoiler" tuning option draws inspiration from the Veneno's spoiler, albeit featuring double mounts and fins. The C-pillar vents appear to be derived from the . The hexagonal exhausts are inspired by the , while the shape of the rear bumper is taken from the . The "Hyper Exit Exhaust" option is also based on the LP 700-4. The tail lights seem to combine features from the Veneno, Aventador, and , while the rear design incorporates aspects from the Sesto Elemento, Veneno, Aventador, and . The rear might have also been influenced by the body kit for the Aventador, which is based on the aesthetics of the Sesto Elemento and Veneno. The headlights are modelled after the .

title: Entity Xf
text: Certain default colour schemes of the car also echo the Sesto Elemento, as they resemble its signature carbon-fibre-and-red coating, although substituting the colour red with orange, potentially alluding to the .

title: Entity Xf
text:
*The "Kisama" livery added in [[GTA Online: The Criminal Enterprises|The Criminal Enterprises]] update is based on a .
**Furthermore, two similar liveries named "Yellow Stripes" and "Street Kisama" are available for the [[Deveste Eight]] and [[Torero XO]], respectively.
*The "Comic Book Racing" livery added in The Criminal Enterprises update is based on the by Andy Blackmore Design.

title: Entity Xf
text: The Zentorno is designed as an exotic high-performance vehicle, with very aggressive styling cues and a low, sloped body for added aerodynamic effects. The front end is largely dominated by the numerous intakes, separated by frames. The bonnet area features four small intakes on the centre and two triangle-shaped details over a carbon-fibre portion near the windscreen. The frontal area features two headlights located in black housings, as well as the manufacturer's emblem located between the lights.

title: Entity Xf
text: The sides of the car denote its aerodynamic profile, featuring concave details above the skirts and inset portions on the doors, together with vertical intakes on the rear fenders and diagonal body lines. Like the [[Infernus]], the Zentorno features scissor doors with rounded mirror shells near the cabin A-pillars. However, these doors do not rotate away from the vehicle body, giving it realistic mechanics. The greenhouse area features coloured front separations behind the A-pillars and carbon-fibre panels on the rear quarters, while the area behind the cabin has two roof intakes leading to the engine bay, two rows of six hexagonal vents on the centre, small vents on the sides and two more vents over the rear tail lamps, finished in carbon fibre.

title: Entity Xf
text:
The rear of the car is predominated by carbon-fibre elements, being the bumper, diffuser, and the separations on the rear vents. A set of red LED strips can be seen on the upper side, with the car's name embossed in chrome letterings between these lights and the two hexagonal exhaust tubes at the bottom. The underside of the car is mostly carbon-plated, with exposed front axle arms, gearbox/diff and rear axle.

Its interior and dial set is shared with the [[Vacca]], itself being a derivative of the one from the [[Banshee]] with yellow dials instead of blue. The manufacturer emblem can be seen on the horn cap.

title: Entity Xf
text: The Zentorno is prominently painted in a primary colour for the body, while the secondary colour is applied on the front bumper trim, the triangle-shaped details on the bonnet area, the lines seen on the vents and around the hexagonal vents on the engine bay, the rear bumper trim and the tyre details of the stock wheels. The car has 10-spoke rims with an angled detail on the ends and a blacked-out appearance.

title: Entity Xf
text: Surprisingly, the Zentorno is very competitive with high-end supercars such as the [[RE-7B]] and [[Tempesta]] around a normal circuit due to its superb cornering speeds. It can also reach fairly high speeds, making it faster than the [[Entity XF]], [[Turismo R]], Infernus, and [[Cheetah]]. The engine in the Zentorno delivers incredibly smooth and alarmingly quick acceleration. In fact, the base stats of the car made it the fastest accelerating supercar in the game (possibly on par with the [[Voltic]]). The car features non-adjustable suspension that is about equal to, if not lower than Competition level, and because it is so close to the ground, the car cannot climb stairs (both forwards and backwards) and can also flip very easily when colliding with sidewalks.

title: Entity Xf
text:
The car's handling is extremely responsive, as it can take corners at high speeds with relative ease due to the lowered suspension and the good weight distribution. But due to the car having such a sensitive handling, It can become a deficit more than a benefit for people using a keyboard as it will turn at 100% power. The high-output engine may also become difficult to control for inexperienced drivers. The vehicle has very minimal oversteer, but it can still spin due to its handling power, but does not always lose control too easily.

The Zentorno's grip can also become a big problem when driving on bumpy roads, if two or more wheels lift off the ground (even for a second), one (or more wheels) will still make such strong contact with the ground for the car to enter a spin. However, the four-wheel drive layout lowers the risk of this, and usually "fixes" itself back into driving forward, picking up speed on the way.

title: Entity Xf
text: Although no physical engine model exists in-game, the website stated that the Zentorno is powered by a 6.8 liter V12 engine that produces 750HP, which is somewhat reflected by the number of hexagonal vents on the rear (similar to how the Sesto Elemento is powered by a V10 engine and features exactly ten hexagonal vents). It has a 6-speed gearbox and an all-wheel drive layout (30% front, 70% rear distribution). The engine sound is typically high-revving, shared with the Cheetah.

*Both vehicles have the same wheels

title: Adder
text: The [[Truffade]] '''Adder''' is a two-door supercar featured in and .

title: Adder
text: The Adder is heavily based on the , as evident by the general shape, greenhouse area, rear fascia, and roof, with a major influence from the by AutoExpress.co.uk, seen primarily in the side profile and some front and rear fascia elements. The front intakes and grille seem to be taken from the , while the headlights have a somewhat similar shape to the , although the layout is similar to . The tail lights are based on typical s, such as the , as they are flattened C-shaped tail lights.

title: Adder
text:
The design of the Adder leans towards a bulky profile in comparison to most supercars, yet retaining aerodynamic features from these. The front bumper features large ducts near the base, featuring chrome trims passing on the upper side and leading to the outer edges. The bumper's bottom edge is raised for the width beneath the main grille, which seems to bear a black/polymer extender on it. The main grille is depicted as a wide, curved trapezium-like element, with the [[Truffade]] emblem mounted centrally on it. On the upper area besides the grille, a set of circular headlamps can be seen on black housings, each one consisting of twin main lamps and an outer turn signal.

The Adder's interior uses the same "Super GT" textures and dials also used on the [[9F]] and [[Rapid GT]], albeit featuring a Truffade emblem on the right-side dashboard, as well as the Truffade 'T' logo on the steering wheel.

title: Adder
text: The Adder is prominently painted in a primary colour for the bodywork and the stitches on the interior, while the secondary colour will be applied in the form of twin stripes on the bonnet and a panel on the rear. Interestingly, the rear panel gives the impression of an apparent pop-up mechanical spoiler (a feature derived from the Bugatti Veyron), but unfortunately, the Adder does not have this feature. The rims have a unique design, consisting of 20 spokes that alternate between wide, semi-curved spokes and thinner, straighter ones.

title: Adder
text:
As befitting the car's real life counterpart, the Adder boasts exceptional engine power, so much that it remains among the best-performing cars in a straight line. However, the car is somewhat sluggish around corners, owing to its prominent understeer. Its poor handling is exacerbated by the absence of a spoiler upgrade. It can be difficult to utilize the Adder’s top speed due to its subpar acceleration, being outpaced by most supercars in that respect. Fortunately, the Adder’s AWD layout partially alleviates these shortcomings, helping to jolt the car forward from a standstill and provide additional stability at high speed.

The large chassis and overall shape gives it a strong and rigid design, which is something the player would want when crashing or colliding. The deformation rate is slow, though the wheels tend to lock up or give a positive camber when done so. The front of the car also has a tendency to "slip" or skitter off other cars it touches when at high speeds.

title: Adder
text:
The Adder's statistical stock top speed is 115 mph / 186 km/h.
*EMS Engine Upgrade 1 produces 117 mph / 188 km/h.
*EMS Engine Upgrade 2 produces 118 mph / 190 km/h.
*EMS Engine Upgrade 3 produces 119 mph / 193 km/h.
*EMS Engine Upgrade 4 produces 121 mph / 194 km/h.
Fully-upgraded, the car tops out at just under 125 mph on flat roads. Although once the fastest supercar in a straight line, it has since strayed far from first position, beaten by over a dozen others ranging from the [[FMJ]], [[Visione]], and [[Tezeract]] up to the [[Banshee 900R]], [[Deveste Eight]], and [[811]].

title: Adder
text: The Adder features two side-by-side engine covers derived from the [[9F]] (albeit laid backwards), intended to emulate the W16 engine from the real-life counterpart. Said engine is coupled to a 6-speed gearbox and is laid out longitudinally in a mid-engine, all-wheel drive layout, giving the car some excellent take off and traction. The engine sound is shared with the 9F, being a high-revving sound with a muffled exhaust note. The website states that the Adder boasts an 8-liter engine, pushing 1100 bhp to the wheels, giving it what was originally stated to be a top speed of 250mph. However, the website as of an enhanced version patch states it can reach up to only 215 mph. In-game, the Adder cannot reach either of these speeds under normal circumstances.

title: Adder
text: Prior to the [[GTA Online: Lowriders|Lowriders]] update, [[Legendary Motorsport]] stated the car was powered by a 8 Liter 1100hp engine capable of pushing the car of up to 250 mph and with a 0-60 mph time of 3 seconds. After the Lowriders update, the car's acclaimed top speed was changed to 215 mph. With the website's refresh after the [[GTA Online: Further Adventures in Finance and Felony|Further Adventures in Finance and Felony]] update, the website no longer states the car's top speed.

Adder
text:
*Can be purchased from [[Legendary Motorsport]] for [[Money|$]]1,000,000.
*Spawns frequently in front of [[Sessanta Nove]] at [[Portola Drive]], [[Rockford Hills]] as a reference to the .

title: Franklin and Lamar
text: '''Franklin and Lamar''' is a mission in , given to [[Franklin Clinton]] by car dealer [[Simeon Yetarian]]. Fellow protagonist [[Michael De Santa]] also makes an appearance in the opening cutscene of the mission.

title: Franklin and Lamar
text: Nine years after the events of the [[Prologue (GTA V)|Prologue]], [[Michael De Santa]] is having a conversation with his therapist, [[Isiah Friedlander|Dr. Isiah Friedlander]]. Michael is growing increasingly unhappy at the fact that he is going through a midlife crisis, beginning to release a small amount of stress by shouting at Dr. Friedlander that the perfect life he dreamt of is disjointed, thus ending their brief session for the day.

title: Franklin and Lamar
text: Michael heads outside and sits on a bench overlooking [[Del Perro Beach]]. This brings him into a chance encounter with [[Lamar Davis]] and [[Franklin Clinton]], who he reluctantly redirects to their repossession location of [[Bertolt Beach House]]. The story then turns to focus on Franklin as he anxiously questions Lamar's motives for proceeding with the repossession, as he doesn't see it as legitimate work. As they sneak onto the property, Franklin is given a choice between reposessing a [[9F Cabrio]] or a [[Rapid GT]]. If the player stays at the house after entering the vehicle, the car owner will pull Franklin from the car and start attacking him.

title: Franklin and Lamar
text: After acquiring the vehicles, Franklin and Lamar engage in a high-speed chase throughout different parts of [[Los Santos (HD Universe)|Los Santos]] using the resposessed vehicles, with Lamar egging on Franklin to push the cars to their limit. If Franklin manages to pass Lamar during the race, he will react negatively, saying "How the fuck did you get ahead of me?". In the beginning of the chase, Franklin urges Lamar to drive carefully since Simeon cuts the cost from the employee's paychecks if the repossessed car is damaged. In return, Lamar suggests Franklin to work for [[JB Bradshaw]]'s [[LSPD Auto Impound|tow business]] if he needs money, to which Franklin refuses, as he does not want to be instrumental for JB and [[Tonya Wiggins|Tonya]] "smoking crack in peace". This dialogue ironically foreshadows Franklin's free help for JB and Tonya to tow vehicles later on in five different occasions starting with the [[Strangers and Freaks|mission]] [[Pulling Favors]], which are caused by JB's drug addiction.

title: Franklin and Lamar
text: Franklin and Lamar end their chase at the [[Union Depository]] car park and exchange repartee with each other. If Franklin's car has sustained heavy damage by this point, Lamar will comment on the state of his vehicle. After hearing [[Los Santos Police Department (HD Universe)|LSPD]] sirens in the distance, the pair drive away in different directions to lose the unwanted police attention. Once the two-star [[Wanted Level in GTA V|wanted level]] is lost, Franklin meets Lamar at the back of the [[Premium Deluxe Motorsport]] dealership, where they witness their boss and owner of the car dealership, [[Simeon Yetarian]], berating a young man, [[Jimmy De Santa]], for making racist comments about him, which in actuality is part of Simeon's scheme to force Jimmy into purchasing a [[BeeJay XL]], something that Lamar himself points out to Franklin. After Franklin and Lamar decide to leave the dealership, Simeon will continue to encourage Jimmy to purchase the car, with Jimmy getting in the car and starting it. When the conversation ends, Simeon tells Franklin to go away.

title: Franklin and Lamar
text: Both Lamar and Franklin leave the dealership and head to Franklin's [[Clinton Residence|house]], where Lamar mocks Franklin's haircut after he's been denied access to Franklin's home. The mission concludes as Franklin walks around the house, which also leads to the brief introduction of his aunt, [[Denise Clinton]], and the basics of the game.

title: Complications
Complications
text: '''Complications''' is a mission in , given to [[Franklin Clinton]] by car dealer [[Simeon Yetarian]] from [[Premium Deluxe Motorsport]] in [[Pillbox Hill]], [[Los Santos (HD Universe)|Los Santos]]. Fellow protagonist [[Michael De Santa]] is also playable during the mission's final sequence.

title: Complications
text:
Simeon is seen arranging a deal with [[Mr. Kenneth]] in the front parking lot right outside his [[Premium Deluxe Motorsport|dealership]] from 8:00 to 18:00. Simeon orders Franklin to repossess a yellow [[Karin]] [[BeeJay XL]] that [[Jimmy De Santa]] bought from him from the [[De Santa Residence]]. Franklin leaves and Simeon continues to negotiate.

Before arriving at the house, Simeon will call Franklin, showing his anger after failing to deliver the [[Bagger]] from the [[Repossession|previous mission]]. Upon arriving, Franklin knocks out the [[Carlos (GTA V)|gardener]] and proceeds to sneak into the house. Franklin needs to navigate the house stealthily to avoid alerting its residents, passing through the kitchen, and entering the garage to steal the SUV. Franklin manages to successfully steal the SUV and drives away from the house back to the dealership.

title: Complications
text:
Suddenly Michael, who was hidden in the SUV's backseat, points a [[Pistol|gun]] at Franklin's head and threatens him, asking him who he is working for and ordering him to continue driving back towards the dealership. Franklin stops near the dealership, and Michael then orders him to drive through the dealership window. A short [[Cutscenes|cutscene]] plays where Michael quickly gives Franklin some [[Money|cash]] and tells him to leave the scene.

The player, now controlling Michael, then has to beat up Simeon. After sufficiently beating Simeon enough, another cutscene is triggered. Michael orders Simeon to leave his son alone and then threatens him not to cross him again.

title: Complications
text: ''"Traffic accidents are common enough in [[Los Santos (HD Universe)|Los Santos]]. Traffic accidents involving parked cars are not uncommon. Traffic accidents involving cars parked inside a dealership are still unusual, however, but that is just what happened yesterday in [[Pillbox Hill]]. A deranged or possibly drunk joyrider drove his car straight into the showroom of Premium Deluxe Motorsport. The owner, Mr. Simeon Yetarian, was injured in the accident, but the driver fled the scene before [[Los Santos Police Department (HD Universe)|cops]] could get there. Mr. Yetarian told our reporter "I am a well-known philanthropist and charity worker as well as an excellent car dealer. Therefore I can only say it is greatly unfortunate that a chubby alcoholic would consider my showroom an acceptable place to crash his car. I am hoping given all the work I do in the community and especially for race relations that the city will help me pay for the damage." A spokesman for the city commented "we have no comment at this time."''

But the owner, Simeon Yetarian, assured police, that this incident was purely an accident, and not a disgruntled customer. One man witnessed the carnage. "It was crazy as hell, that dude must've been tweakin', I know I am. You got a washing machine I could take apart?"''

Complications
text:
*If the FPS is set too high during this mission, the [[Premier]] will shift positions slightly before [[Mr. Kenneth]] enters it, and as a result, [[Simeon Yetarian|Simeon]]'s right hand will be clipping into the Premier's roof while his left hand is resting in mid-air instead of the car's door.
**If the FPS is higher than 120, then the Premier will shift positions so much that it will automatically trigger a mission failure (with the reason being that Simeon's deal was disrupted), making it impossible to progress in this mission. 
***This was fixed with the [[GTA Online: Money Fronts|Money Fronts]] update.
*If [[Franklin Clinton|Franklin]] knocks out the [[Carlos (GTA V)|gardener]] with a stealth attack, it may still be added to his People Killed [[Statistics in GTA V|stats]].
*If Franklin looks in the back seat before entering the [[BeeJay XL|car]], it is possible to see a red blanket laid down across the seat (where Michael is hiding), although Michael cannot be made to trigger until Franklin gets into the car. Once Michael emerges, however, the red blanket will disappear completely.
*If the player uses Franklin's [[Special Ability|special ability]] when [[Michael De Santa|Michael]] sits up and puts the gun against his head, the BeeJay XL will catapult forward.
*When Michael places a [[Pistol|handgun]] to Franklin's head in the car, he refers to the gun as a 9mm, although in [[Ammu-Nation (HD Universe)|Ammu-Nation]], the gun's description says it's a .45 caliber. This is a mistake on Ammu-Nation's part as the weapon in question is based on the , which is chambered in 9mm.
*After the [[Cutscenes|cutscene]] in which Michael orders Franklin to ram the SUV through the window, the vehicle's horn sound may change.
*During the fistfight with Simeon, he may say to Michael three possible quotes: "See, now. You've pissed me off.", "Simeon Yetarian doesn't back down from anybody.", or "I won't be treated like this." None of these quotes will appear in the subtitles if they are enabled.
*At the conclusion of the mission, Michael can re-enter the [[Premium Deluxe Motorsport|dealership]] and take any of the cars on display. Strangely, however, if the player saves a car in their [[Garages|garage]], the vehicle will despawn the next time the player enters the garage.
**Coincidentally, Jimmy's crashed BeeJay XL will still be at the dealership and can be driven by the player. Unlike the vehicles stolen from the showroom, Jimmy's crashed BeeJay XL can be kept and it will be automatically repaired. However, like the vehicles inside the dealership, the BeeJay XL will disappear from the player's garage. This has been fixed in the [[Grand Theft Auto V: Enhanced Edition|enhanced version]].
*After completing the mission and heading to Michael's house as Michael, Franklin's [[Buffalo S]] may appear to still be there. It can be saved in Michael's garage. The car may appear at the place even if Franklin used any other car, but the mission's been replayed. If Michael takes a ride in Franklin's car (e.g. attempting to return the Buffalo to its owner), the latter would call Michael, asking him "what the fuck" he is doing with his car.

title: Complications
text: *The gold medal objective "Can't Touch This" is likely a reference to the song "".

title: Complications
text:
*If the mission is started during the day, the Premier that Mr. Kenneth is attempting to purchase will be red. However, if it is started at night, the car will be yellow once the timelapse is finished.
*If Franklin enters the dealership and looks inside Simeon's office at the beginning of the mission, one will discover that Simeon already replaced Franklin's Employee of the Month plaque with one dedicated to himself.
*During the mission, two [[Tailgater]]s (one gray and one white) can be found parked outside the dealership. Franklin can choose one of them to drive to Michael's [[De Santa Residence|house]], and Michael can use one of them once the mission is complete.
*If Franklin ignores Simeon's phone call on the way to Michael's house, he will send Franklin a text message mentioning the locked garage and his suspicions of Franklin keeping the [[Bagger|motorbike]].
*During the confrontation with Simeon, Michael will claim that the latter sold the [[BeeJay XL]] to Jimmy for $5,000 a month. In , the SUV could originally be bought from [[Southern San Andreas Super Autos]] for $27,000 flat before it was removed from the in-game website in the [[GTA Online: San Andreas Mercenaries|San Andreas Mercenaries]] update.
*At the end of the cutscene with Michael beating up Simeon, Michael throws Simeon onto the floor. However, Simeon disappears after the cutscene is finished.
*Using stealth, it's possible to explore the mansion without being spotted. Aside from [[Amanda De Santa|Amanda]] flirting with her [[tennis]] [[Kyle Chavis|coach]] in the kitchen, [[Jimmy De Santa|Jimmy]] can be observed in his room playing video games, and [[Tracey De Santa|Tracey]] will be lying on her bed, talking on the phone with her friend [[Lara (GTA V)|Lara]] (but her back will be conveniently facing the door). Jimmy is so distracted by the game, it's actually possible for Franklin to stand in the doorway and not be noticed.
**Approaching any resident of Michael's house will result in a unique mission fail cutscene.
*After the phone call to Simeon once the player enters the SUV is finished, Franklin will be unable to use his [[Mobile Phone|cell phone]] until the mission is complete.
*If the player damages [[Jimmy De Santa|Jimmy]]'s car before entering it, Michael will stand up immediately when Franklin enters the car. This will skip a phone call between Franklin and Simeon and change Michael's quote from ''"You just keep driving where you're going."'' to ''"Take me where you were going."''
**This will also happen if Franklin tries to exit the car before making the phone call.
*When getting back to the dealership while Michael holds Franklin at gunpoint, [[First-Person View|first-person mode]] is disabled as Franklin is forced to look forward. If the player enters the SUV while first-person mode is active, the camera will automatically switch to [[Third-Person View|third-person mode]] when Michael points his pistol at Franklin's head. First-person view will be restored during the fistfight with Simeon.
*If the player drives too far from the dealership or goes a different way to the way Michael wants Franklin to go, he will knock Franklin out by hitting his right temple with his pistol and the mission will fail.
*When the player crashes into Simeon's dealership, the BeeJay XL they are driving has a noticeably more aggressive engine tone. This is due to a unique sound effect played over the scene.
*During Franklin's phone call to Lamar upon completion of the mission, a topless black [[Mesa]] can be found parked behind him. It can be taken afterwards.
*In the [[Beta Content in GTA V|beta version]], Franklin was going to climb the vines to get into Michael's house.

title: Clinton Residence
text: The '''Clinton Residence''' (also known as the '''Forum Drive safehouse''') is the first [[Safehouses in GTA V|safehouse]] used by [[protagonist]] [[Franklin Clinton]] in , and also appears in .

title: Clinton Residence
text: The safehouse is located on [[Forum Drive]], [[Strawberry]], and is unlocked after [[Franklin and Lamar]].

title: Clinton Residence
text: The safehouse is a single-story bungalow where the player can save their game in Franklin's bedroom, which is located at the first door to the left of the front door. Across the hallway is a small living room with a watchable television and a supply of joints that Franklin can take a hit from. The living room leads on to a small kitchen, where Franklin can [[Drinking|drink]] a beer or use a [[Health|first aid kit]]. A door leading to the back garden can be found in the kitchen, but cannot be used. The interior of the house is characterized by its retro design and decorated with various spiritual and tribal ornaments and artwork. A garage can be found to the left of the property, which is large enough to store one car and one motorcycle (Franklin's [[Buffalo S]] and a [[Bagger]] obtained in an early mission spawn in the driveway). Following [[The Hotel Assassination]], if the player enters the house using cheats or in [[Director Mode]], Franklin's bedroom is cleared out (since he moved to [[Vinewood Hills]]). Chop's kennel can be found in the back garden. The [[Radio Stations in GTA V|radio station]] playing inside the house is [[Radio Los Santos]].

title: Clinton Residence
text: At the beginning of the game, [[Franklin Clinton]] lives here with his aunt [[Denise Clinton|Denise]], after they inherited the house in Franklin's grandmother's will. A short time later, Franklin agrees to take care of [[Chop]], a [[Dogs|Rottweiler]] belonging to his friend [[Lamar Davis]], and Chop soon starts living at the house with Franklin and Denise.

title: Clinton Residence
text: Following Franklin's move to [[3671 Whispymound Drive]] in [[Vinewood Hills]] after the completion of [[The Hotel Assassination]], the house is turned into a "center for women" by [[Denise Clinton]] and both the house and garage are made inaccessible to the player ([[PlayStation 3|PS3]]/[[Xbox 360]]). In the [[Grand Theft Auto V: Enhanced Edition|enhanced]] and [[Grand Theft Auto V and Online: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S Editions|expanded & enhanced]] versions of the game, the garage remains accessible to the player, but the house still cannot be accessed. After Franklin moves out, Denise will send him an email barring him from re-entering the house. Once he has replied, Franklin tells her that the "only mistake" that his mother made was giving her the house and he tells Denise to stay away from him.

title: Clinton Residence
text: After Franklin moves to his new safehouse, he can sometimes be seen on Forum Drive driving away from the house, indicating that he was returning to retrieve some of his belongings or to make sure his aunt hadn't done anything drastic to the house. If he returns to the house, the front door will be locked and Denise will shout from inside, telling Franklin to go away. The two may exchange a few words.

title: Clinton Residence
text: The house plays no role in the storyline of ''Grand Theft Auto Online''. However, it is mentioned by Franklin and Lamar that Denise still resides in this house in [[2021]].

text: *In the [[Grand Theft Auto V: Enhanced Edition|enhanced edition]], walking from the living room to the kitchen can pause whatever is on the TV. Returning to the living room or front door should fix it.

title: Clinton Residence
text:
*If the player fires a weapon at the house as [[Michael De Santa|Michael]] or [[Trevor Philips|Trevor]], [[Denise Clinton|Denise]] can be heard inside complaining and shouting. If the player continues, [[Franklin Clinton|Franklin]] will eventually call or text them to stop firing.
**Even after moving into [[3671 Whispymound Drive]] (and the following eviction of Franklin from the house), Franklin will still call Michael or Trevor if they shoot at the house.
*It is possible to access the interior of the safehouse after Franklin moves out, by going to the roof of the house, [[Switch Scenes|switching]] to another character and then switching back. The player spawns inside; however, they cannot save the game, even if playing as Franklin. This is not the case in the [[Grand Theft Auto V: Enhanced Edition|enhanced version]].
**Franklin can still interact with Denise; Michael cannot interact with her since they never [[canon]]ically met; Trevor also cannot interact with Denise despite [[Hood Safari|having previously met her]].
*For all characters, but more relevantly Franklin, if the player manages to get into the house after Franklin being evicted, they can still find Denise inside. Denise's presence or lack thereof is not synchronous with her annoyed exchange she has when Franklin "trespasses" and there will be no indication of the house's supposed conversion into a "women's centre" or even any other women besides Denise.
*A [[Bleeter]] post from Denise incorrectly states that the house is in [[Davis]].
*If the player enters the house (e.g. using mods) after Franklin no longer lives there, they will see that:
**Franklin's bedroom is now relatively bare.
**Franklin is still able to [[Drinking|drink]] beer in the kitchen and collect the two [[health]] pickups located in the house.
**All [[protagonist]]s are able to use the TV, as with any other safehouse.
*A picture in the house shows a young Franklin at [[BJ Smith Recreational Center]] wearing a [[Los Santos Panic]] top. This is likely an oversight because the [[Ballas (HD Universe)|Ballas]] support that team, whereas Franklin has always been associated with [[The Families]].

It was made available for purchase in ''Grand Theft Auto Online'' during the [[Gun Van Week]], as part of the continuation of the [[GTA Online: Los Santos Drug Wars|Los Santos Drug Wars]] update.

title: Railgun
text: A railgun is a weapon that fires inert metallic rounds at velocities higher than the speed of sound using an electromagnetic effect. As such, it has incredible range and accuracy in addition to massive kinetic energy. However, at the time the weapon was introduced, railguns are still considered to be prototype phase and due to a myriad of issues, such as power generation and heat dissipation are limited in size and portability to fixed (usually naval) mountings. Portable railguns do not exist outside of theoretical models.

title: Railgun
text:
The Railgun is a high-tech military prototype weapon designed for infantry use, adopting a carbine-like appearance. It bears a strong resemblance to the featured in the ''Halo'' series.

The weapon features a very linear design easily distinguished by two electrically-powered rails on the front, the vented units on either side of the gun just behind the power source, and a small fixed stock on the rear. The Railgun also has a transparent sight on top with a triangle-shaped reticle on it. A green light is visible when the Railgun is loaded and turns red when fired.

According to the text on the side of the weapon, the Railgun is property of the [[United States of America|United States]] Government.

title: Railgun
text: When equipped, the Railgun emits a low pitch humming sound, which can be more easily heard when in first-person view. When fired, a flash of electric arc can be seen in the barrel, in which it will be followed by a small explosion in the muzzle (a sonic boom) after the rounds are fired. Attempting to fire the weapon without ammunition will produce a unique static sound, as opposed to the standard "click" of conventional weapons. In ''GTA Online'', the Railgun has a higher pitched humming sound and lacks the unload charging sound.

title: Railgun
text:
The Railgun fires rounds at the speed of 2000 m/s (7200 KPH), which is the same velocity as most weapons. In real life, the rounds travel much faster than regular firearm bullets due to their supersonic velocity. On impact, the kinetic energy rounds are capable of causing massive damage, which are on par with the [[RPG]]. That is, it can destroy any unarmored vehicle in one shot.

However, this weapon requires accurate shooting because of its poor blast radius; any shot that missed deals no damage, especially when one hits a vehicle's window and the projectile can easily pass through both open side doors of a helicopter. Its blast radius is only one meter.

title: Railgun
text:
Since it is a single-shot and it takes multiple seconds to recharge, this weapon is good at dealing with enemy vehicles, but is less effective against groups of enemies on foot. It is also an effective backup weapon to be used in missions that involve heavy shootouts, such as [[Heists]]. When used from low cover, the gun takes less time to recharge, ideal for taking out enemies from areas where they cannot flank the player easily.

The gun also has a maximum range of 500 meters, being ideal for long-range application (only surpassed by sniper rifles, which have a maximum range of 1,500 meters). However, its lock-on range is very limited, at only 40 meters (compared to assault rifles, which have a lock-on range of 65 meters).

title: Railgun
text: Based on the markings of the gun, it has an energy capacity of 1.21 gigawatts. The [[Rockstar Games Social Club]] website also indicates the Railgun is a fully-automatic weapon, yet it is a single-shot weapon in-game. Assuming that the weapon is limited by the single-round magazine, it would mechanically have fully-automatic capabilities.

title: Railgun
text: Previously only available in select [[Missions in GTA Online|missions]] and gamemodes, the Railgun becomes freely available in as part of the [[GTA Online: Los Santos Drug Wars|Los Santos Drug Wars]] update, available for purchase at the [[Gun Van]]. However the weapon’s performance have been reduced. The projectile velocity has been lowered from 2000 m/s (7200 KPH) to 750 m/s (2700 KPH), and inflicts less damage to players and vehicles. The Railgun can kill some players with a single round, but those who are at least Rank 100 will survive with only a sliver of health remaining, and after that they are likely to be wasted from fall damage, unless they are equipped with Super Heavy [[Body Armor|Armor]], in which case it would take two shots to take them out. It can also destroy unarmored vehicles in one shot, and may be a effective weapon against maneuverable aircraft, although the projectile is slow and only has a range of 500 meters. The weapon cannot lock-on to enemies or vehicles.

title: Railgun
text:
Against vehicles, the Railgun does slightly more damage than explosive rounds fired from the [[Heavy Sniper Mk II]] and [[Pump Shotgun Mk II]] (12.5% more than the aforementioned weapons). It can instantly destroy an unarmored vehicle even if a player is inside (as opposed to two explosive rounds to blow it up). The damage appears to have 45% of the [[RPG]]'s, requiring 20 shots to destroy a heavily armored [[Personal Vehicles|Personal Vehicle]] (namely the [[Insurgent Pick-Up Custom]] and [[Nightshark]]), and nine shots to destroy the [[Rhino (HD Universe)|Rhino Tank]].

In the files, the updated model appears to have some of its flags removed, namely the ones that allows the original model to lock on most targets and its ability to be used in a vehicle in ''Grand Theft Auto Online''.

text:
*Can be bought from [[Ammu-Nation (HD Universe)|Ammu-Nation]] for $250,000 after completing [[Minor Turbulence]].
*One can be found within the underwater [[Wrecks|wreckage]] of the [[Cargo Plane|cargo plane]] from Minor Turbulence, located north of [[Stab City]].

title: Railgun
text:
*Can be bought from the [[Gun Van]] if it is in stock for $730,000, less the applicable discount<!--Gun Van stock is always discounted-->.

Additionally, the Railgun can be found and used in some [[Adversary Modes]] and also [[Supplies/Steal Missions#Railgun|a Bunker Supplies/Steal Mission]], though they cannot be kept afterward unless the player already owns one.

title: Railgun
text:
*Part of a [[Bunker Resupply]] mission where one must be stolen from [[Humane Labs and Research]] or [[Los Santos Naval Port]]. During this, the player can freely use the Railgun until the mission is complete or the weapon is destroyed.
*[[Merryweather Security]] guards in [[The Doomsday Heist]] missions and [[Freemode]] [[Business Battles]] are sometimes armed with Railguns.
*Multiple Railguns can be found inside the bunker during [[The Data Contract/Finale|The Data Contract]].

title: Railgun
text: *The Railgun's power of "1.21 Gigawatts" is a reference to the '''' film trilogy, being the amount of energy required for the DeLorean time machine to time travel.

title: Railgun
text: *From November 18, 2014, to July 19, 2021, the Railgun was exclusive to returning players, but as of July 20, 2021, it is available for all players to purchase in ''GTA V''.

title: Railgun
text:
*When using the Railgun during Beast vs. Slasher, the lights on the gun will not be turned on until the power is restored.
*Two Railguns can be seen in the back of the [[TM-02 Khanjali]]. However, they are unusable.

title: Railgun
text:
*The [[GTA Online: Arena War|Arena War]] update introduced an issue in ''GTA V'' whereby legitimately purchased or salvaged Railguns will disappear from the protagonist's inventory whenever switching characters or reloading the game. This may be an unintended impact of an exploit fix for the weapon in ''GTA Online'' where it is not supposed to be able to be kept outside the jobs. This bug has been fixed with [[GTA Online: The Diamond Casino & Resort|The Diamond Casino & Resort]] update.
*In third-person view, the coils of the weapon always remain in red instead of turning to green when the weapon is loaded. In first-person view, however, the coils correctly turn to green or red depending if the weapon is loaded or not.
*The projectile may go through the vehicle without exploding when it hits the windows.

title: Mr. Philips
Mr. Philips
text: After Franklin meets Michael at his house, they each have a drink to celebrate [[The Jewel Store Job|their successful heist]]. While they discuss business, [[Dave Norton]], the [[FIB]] agent who [[Prologue (GTA V)|offered]] him a deal then appears out of the blue and warns Michael that his involvement in the heist has alerted the FIB and may alert his former associate, [[Trevor Philips]]. Unconcerned by this, Michael brushes this aside by claiming that Trevor must be dead, before denying any involvement in the heist. Dave switches the television on to watch a news reporter interviewing the [[Albert Stalley|police officer]] Michael threatened outside the [[Vangelico|jewelry store]]. Michael switches the television off and again denies any involvement in the heist.

title: Mr. Philips
text: Unbeknownst to Michael, Trevor is still alive. He overhears the news report while having sex with [[Ashley Butler]] in his [[Trevor's Trailer|trailer]] in [[Sandy Shores]]. The police officer being interviewed mentions a phrase used by one of the robbers: "''You forget a thousand things everyday, make sure this is one of them.''" Trevor instantly recognizes this as a phrase often used by Michael. Shocked by this, Trevor zips up his pants, grabs a [[Pisswasser|beer]] and walks out of the trailer, encountering [[The Lost MC|Lost MC]] leader [[Johnny Klebitz]] who is angry at Trevor for again having sex with Ashley. Trevor ignores Johnny as [[Wade Hebert]] and [[Ron Jakowski]] attempt to restrain him.

title: Mr. Philips
text:
A still shocked and confused Trevor continues to walk away with Johnny walking after him expressing his anger. Trevor eventually snaps and fires several insults at Johnny, before sarcastically telling Johnny to drop his pants so that they can have sex, believing that is the reason for his anger.

An emotionally drained Johnny calms down, admitting to Trevor that he still loves Ashley. After feigning an attempt to console Johnny, Trevor grabs him by the throat and shoves him to the ground before smashing the beer bottle against his head and repeatedly stamping on it, killing him. After telling Johnny to get up before realizing he is dead, Trevor, Ron and Wade head off to Trevor's [[Bodhi|truck]], leaving a tearful Ashley to cradle Johnny's corpse.

title: Mr. Philips
text: Knowing that the rest of the Lost will be very angry over their leader's death, Trevor decides to wipe out the local chapter of The Lost M.C. and their [[meth]] business from [[Blaine County]], before they have a chance to exact revenge. He drives with Wade and Ron to a [[R L Hunter & Sons|Lost hangout]] in [[Grapeseed]] where Terry Thorpe, Clay Simons, and other members of the Lost are hanging about. After Trevor announces and mocks Johnny's death, the members of The Lost retreat to their [[The Range|trailer park]] to notify the rest of the gang. Trevor follows them there and brutally kills the whole gang in his psychotic rage, including Terry and Clay.

title: Mr. Philips
text: Afterwards, Trevor orders Wade to begin looking for Michael Townley, the "ghost" in [[Los Santos (HD Universe)|Los Santos]], and drives with Ron to a [[Ortega's Trailer|trailer]] belonging to the [[Varrios Los Aztecas (HD Universe)|Aztecas]] leader, [[Ortega]]. After pushing Ortega's trailer into the [[Zancudo River|adjacent river]], Trevor can kill or spare Ortega, solidifying his new position as Blaine County's meth dealing and illegal firearms trading kingpin. Sparing Ortega will make him reappear as another thug in [[Trevor Philips Industries]], killing him will not, and replaying the mission later on will have the game treat it as if the player spared him regardless.
